title: Families on Stelae
short: Stelae list relatives with "his son", "his daughter", "born of" (jr.n, ms.n) and their epithets.
trouble: Students read jr.n NN as "NN made". Here it means "whom NN made" (bore): the mother's name follows.

blocks.html: Many stelae name not only their owner but his family: parents, wife, children, sometimes servants. The phrases are few and fixed, and they use grammar you now know: participles (Passive Participles) and relative forms (Relative Forms).
Family phrases to know: zꜣ=f mrj=f "his beloved son", zꜣt=f mrt=f "his beloved daughter", ḥmt=f mrt=f "his beloved wife", nbt-pr "lady of the house", and ms.n or jr.n + a woman's name, "born of …".

mrj=f is a passive participle with a suffix, "beloved of him", so zꜣ=f mrj=f is "his son, his beloved one". ms.n is a relative form of msj "give birth": "whom (she) bore". The mother's name follows as the subject: ms.n nbt-pr nfrt "whom the lady of the house Nefret bore", that is, "born of the lady of the house Nefret". jr.n, "whom (she) made", says the same thing. Egyptians traced people through their mothers on these monuments as a matter of course.

blocks.title: A son and his mother
blocks.q: Translate zꜣ=f jtj jr.n nbt-pr ḥnwt.
steps: zꜣ=f "his son", then the son's name jtj "Iti".
jr.n: a relative form, "whom … made", with the mother as subject.
nbt-pr ḥnwt "the lady of the house Henut".
blocks.a: "His son Iti, born of the lady of the house Henut."

blocks.title: Write it
steps: The relative form ms.n, then the mother's name mrt as its subject.

blocks.html: The names on this page, Ameny, Iti, Nefret, Henut and Meret, are common names of the period, chosen as examples; they do not refer to particular stelae. A real stela may list a dozen relatives, each with a title, a name and mꜣꜥ-ḫrw, arranged in rows under the main scene.

Reading jr.n NN as "NN made (it)", as if the woman made the stela. Here jr.n is a relative form describing the person just named: "whom NN made", meaning "born of NN". Check: is a woman's name right after jr.n or ms.n, following someone's name? Then read "born of".
